col.title: Title
col.name: Name
home.nothingNeedsYou: Nothing needs you. Tasks that need a reply, logins to reconnect and change requests to review appear here.
home.nothingRunning: No task is running. Label an issue or ask in Chat.
setup.intro: Set up {tenant}: do these in order. When the last step is done, the first task appears and this page becomes your dashboard. Nothing is installed in your repositories.
setup.step1: 1 · Link GitHub and install the App
setup.step1Done: Linked as {login}. Installed on {account} · {n} repositories selected
setup.step1Todo: Link your GitHub account, then install the GitHub App on the account that owns your repositories.
setup.step2Detail: An empty repository you own, {repo}. Triggers, skills and projects live here.
setup.step3Detail: Use your subscription or an API key.
setup.step4Detail: Pick the template “labeled issue → agent → pull requests with green checks” and the repository. sanchoris opens a pull request with it on your config repository. Merge it on GitHub.
setup.step5Detail: Add the label to an issue. The first task starts.
setup.projectDetail: Group repositories that one agent works on together, such as a frontend and a backend.
setup.slackDetail: Ask for work from a channel or DM.
setup.connectSubscriptionDetail: Run this on your machine and sign in. The login is registered with your account.
setup.name: Name
setup.usedBySessionDetail: A session names the credential it uses. Name it here when you save it.
triggers.intro: A trigger starts a task: an agent session that must run its required skills to the end. {n} triggers, {changes} change request open. A chat trigger names the scope of the chat: all projects, or one project.
triggers.issueLabeled: A GitHub issue gets the label {labels} from {senders}.
triggers.issueComment: A comment is added to a GitHub issue by {senders}.
triggers.children: Children: depth {depth}, up to {count} per task.
triggers.checkRun: A GitHub check run fails on a pull request in {repos}
triggers.webMessage: A message in Web chat with the scope {scope}
triggers.labelNotAllowed: label added by {login}, who is not in the pattern
triggers.senderNotAllowed: sent by {login}, who is not in the pattern
triggers.duplicate: a task with the same name exists
triggers.noEvents: No events yet. Events appear when a trigger receives an issue, a message or a schedule.
triggers.empty: No triggers yet. Use New from template to open a pull request on your config repository.
triggers.footer: Triggers are YAML in your config repositories. Edit them on GitHub. The On switch is the state of the trigger (ENABLED, DISABLED).
triggers.proposed: Opened change request {link}. Merge it on GitHub.
skills.intro: A skill is a procedure the agent can call. A reliable skill runs its fixed steps outside the session, so it finishes the same way every time.
skills.empty: No skills yet. Add a folder under skills/ in your config repository.
skills.footer: Skills are folders in your config repository: {skillMd} for the agent, and {skillYaml} for the steps sanchoris runs. A skill without {skillYaml} is plain: the agent reads it, and a trigger cannot require it.
skill.plainNote: This skill is plain: it has SKILL.md only, so the agent reads it and no steps run.
chat.scopeAllDetail: Starts in {repos}. Can look at every repository and file issues in any of them.
chat.pickScope: Pick a scope to start the chat.
chat.noScopes: No chat trigger is on. A chat starts in the scope of an enabled trigger with source web; add one to your config from
chat.threadLine: Task started by the trigger {trigger} · scope: {scope} · one agent session {session} in {repos}, {run}
chat.issuesFiledDetail: Each issue started its own task, asynchronously.
chat.filedHint: Issues the agent files from a chat appear here. Each one starts its own task.
tasks.intro: {n} tasks. Needs-you items come first. Each task shows where its required skill stands.
tasks.empty: Tasks are empty. Label an issue, or ask in Chat.
task.nudgesExhausted: {skill} did not succeed after the reminders
task.usageLimitManual: Usage limit reached; resume by hand
task.workspaceStopped: The workspace stopped before the task finished
task.messageGoes: Your message goes to the agent session, and the skill runs again.
task.messagePlaceholder: Skip the flaky test and fix the cause in the cart fixture.
task.noSkillRuns: The agent has not called a skill yet.
run.title: Run {n}
run.rateLimitAllowed: the worker's usage is within its limit
run.rateLimitWarning: the worker's usage is close to its limit
run.rateLimitRejected: the worker reached its usage limit
run.rateLimitOther: the worker reported usage limit status {status}
integrations.intro: Your GitHub account, the GitHub App and Slack: the places work comes from and reports to.
integrations.linkedAs: Linked as {login}. sanchoris matches a GitHub user to a member by this login, so a session can use the credential of the member who asked.
integrations.notLinked: Link your GitHub account so sanchoris can match your GitHub activity to you.
integrations.notInstalled: Install the GitHub App on the account that owns your repositories.
integrations.slackDetail: Ask for work from a channel or DM. Optional.
config.intro: Git repositories that hold your triggers, skills and projects. Edit and review changes on GitHub.
config.removeHint: To remove a config, remove its repository from the GitHub App installation on GitHub. The config is then disabled: its triggers stop, its sessions and projects leave these screens, and its unfinished tasks are stopped.
config.disabledHint: The config no longer syncs or starts tasks. Add the repository to the GitHub App installation again and add it as a new config to use it.
config.projectsDetail: A project groups repositories that one agent works on together. A session on a single repository names the repository and needs no project.
credentials.intro: Claude and Codex logins and keys. Each has a name that sessions refer to.
credentials.empty: No credentials yet. Connect a subscription or save an API key.
credentials.howPicked: How a session picks a credential
credentials.howPickedDetail: A session names the credential it uses, for example {example}. Writing {requester} uses the personal credential of the member who asked, and fails if that member has none.
members.intro: {n} of {total} members in {tenant}. Invitations count while they are pending.
members.introNoLimit: {n} members in {tenant}, with no limit. Invitations count while they are pending.
members.footer: Owners and admins invite, change roles and remove members. A session names the credential it uses, so members do not need their own.
audit.intro: Who did what in {tenant}. Entries are append-only. Owners and admins can read and export them.
billing.intro: Plan and usage for {tenant}. Paid plans are billed monthly in USD through Stripe.
billing.adminIntro: {tenant} is on the Admin plan, which a tenant gets when a verified @sancode.dev email creates it. Tasks, workspace hours and members have no limit, nothing is billed, and the plan does not change.
billing.thresholds: you are told at 80% · new tasks wait at 100%
billing.footer: The price covers the whole tenant, whatever the number of members. One task is one issue, one chat thread, or one scheduled run. Workspace hours count the time a workspace is running, not the time a task waits. Change or cancel the plan at any time. Agents run on your own Claude and Codex subscriptions or API keys, so model usage is not billed here. Invoices and the payment method are in Stripe.
operator.intro: {n} tenants · {runs} runs now · {hours} run hours and {revenue} revenue this month. Create, suspend and bill customers. Visible to the operator only.
operator.notOperator: This page is for sanchoris operators.
tenantNew.title: Create tenant
tenantNew.intro: A tenant is the place where your team’s tasks, triggers and billing live. You can invite people after it exists.
tenantNew.limitsTotal: {tasks} tasks and {hours} workspace hours in total
tenantNew.noLimits: no limit on tasks, workspace hours or members
tenantNew.createAndPay: Create tenant and pay in Stripe
tenantNew.afterPayment: After payment you install the GitHub App and connect Claude or Codex.
tenantNew.afterCreate: The tenant is created at once. Next you install the GitHub App and connect Claude or Codex.
login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Sign in with your Google account. You link GitHub later, in Settings.
login.after: New here? Signing in creates your account, and then you create a tenant or join one.
login.failed: Sign-in failed: {error}. Going back to sign in…
